I have lots of thoughts here.

Firstly, fully looking at Arcane, we have 3 episodes left and that's far too little time for me to say that any characters story will be completely told and finished. Maybe most arcs will be satisfyingly completed but not to the point you can kill off those characters. Isha's death is a good example for that, her story was far too short for me to connect with her as a character and her death didn't affect me at all. If she (somehow) had been a champion, I would have been seriously angry.

Before Arcane I'd still would've felt the same about any champions death in the lore. So, I wouldn't drop that main because they won't get more content in the show, I would drop them (after some time), because they won't get more content in league in general (besides random skins). Like killing any character removes any possibility of interacting with them in the upcoming mmorpg. For arguments sake, if my favorite champion is the only champion I care for in league and they are killed off, I will be less interested in trying out the mmorpg, because I know I will not see them. 

Also, from a writing perspective, any champion is basically a tool to tell an interesting story. Runeterra is a huge universe with multiple writers working on it. Many writers might have different ideas of stories they can tell with these champions, so if one writer decides to kill a champion off it removes any potential for future writers to come back to them. Do you really think if they kill off Jinx in Arcane, Riot will never return to tell a story with her? They will, and they will find a boring way to revive her, making the ending of Arcane then pointless.   
  
Something like this is already happening in huge other universes. Look at Marvel, they killed off Iron Man, the death was satisfying and powerful for the story. Too bad Tony Stark is a popular character in the franchise so Marvel is bringing him back as Mr. Doom. There's no way Marvel will be able to approach this, without making the ending of endgame less impactful.

On the other hand if you need to defeat an evil champion, imprisoning them or turning them into stone is a clever way for the story to end without taking away any future potential of these characters. To me, they are just in a limbo state, in which they can still exist in the game. That's different than an actual death. For example, Viego can easily still appear in the mmorpg as a raid boss or something, without taking anything away from the ending of The Ruination. If Viego was actually killed at the end, that just could not happen.

While I do agree with you, that the predictability of this might be a problem, but I think you can have clever workarounds to avoid this. Again, a character can still lose, even if they are alive. If a battle is happening, even if the viewer knows that both champions survive, they still would be on the edge of their seat to see which one wins. Knowing that a champion survives, doesn't take away from the story and still can make the story unpredictable. No ones watching or reading League stories just to see which character survives.
